examples: He looked unhappy with the result.

uncle.definition: The brother of one of your parents; a male relative.
examples: My uncle told funny stories.
We stayed with my paternal uncle during vacation.

uncanny.definition: Strange or mysterious in a way that seems beyond understanding.
examples: She had an uncanny ability to predict the weather.

unearthly.definition: Very strange or unnatural; not fitting in this world.
examples: The glow in the cave gave it an unearthly look.

unsaid.definition: Not spoken; kept private or not expressed
examples: There was an unsaid tension between them.
Her unsaid concern showed in her silence.

unspoken.definition: Not said, but understood or felt by people
examples: Their unspoken agreement saved time.
There were many unspoken worries in the room.

unwelcoming.definition: Not friendly or not ready to accept visitors
examples: The store had an unwelcoming atmosphere.
He gave an unwelcoming response.

unravel.definition: To become clear by solving parts of a complex situation, or to come apart gradually
examples: Investigators worked to unravel the mystery.
The rope unraveled as we pulled it.

unctionless.definition: Lacking warmth, sincerity, or spiritual meaning; sounding empty or unconvincing
examples: His talk felt unctionless and failed to inspire the audience.
The speech was unctionless, with no real message.

unseasoned.definition: Not experienced or not trained; also, not mixed or flavored with seasoning
examples: He sounded unseasoned during the interview.
An unseasoned soup needs salt and spices.

unschooled.definition: Not taught formally; lacking school education
examples: She was unschooled but learned through practice.
He is unschooled in advanced math concepts.
The dog barked at the unwonted sound.
She noticed unwonted quiet in the house.

unverifiable.definition: Impossible to confirm or prove because there is no reliable evidence
examples: The claim is unverifiable, so we can’t include it.
Her story was unverifiable.

uneasy.definition: Slightly worried or uncomfortable; not at ease
examples: I felt uneasy about the last-minute changes.
The team looked uneasy after the warning.

unrelenting.definition: Not stopping or becoming less strong; continuing without pause
examples: They faced unrelenting criticism.
The unrelenting rain ruined the event.

unease.definition: A feeling of worry or discomfort
examples: She felt unease when she saw the broken lock.
There was unease among the group after the incident.

ungird.definition: To remove a belt or strap; also, to loosen or take away restraint
examples: He un gird ed his sword belt before sleeping.
She un gird ed herself from the old responsibilities.
